feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital leadership roles: the experience progression is clear, the scope is substantial, and the public-sector specialization comes through well. It reads polished and modern, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies and opportunities to sharpen impact through clearer outcomes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, showing increasing leadership, ownership, and scope across digital, analytics, web, and multimedia.  
- Strong credibility through concrete scale signals: 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, named tools/platforms, and visible technical depth.  
- Well-positioned executive profile and competencies that align tightly with digital platform, communications systems, and modernization roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition across Header, Core Competencies, Topline Skills, Technical + IT, and Recent Projects; several themes/tools appear multiple times, which weakens concision.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements beyond responsibilities: quantify improvements in engagement, efficiency, adoption, cost savings, search performance, or campaign results where possible.  
- Fix stylistic inconsistencies: “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s,” mixed list punctuation, “social, and multimedia” (remove comma), and title casing/name styling (“Coleman DAVIS” may look inconsistent unless intentional). No major misspellings found; grammar is generally strong.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus, but it reads slightly generic and repeats several competency areas listed elsewhere. It would be stronger with one concrete scale signal and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms” with a more active, executive framing such as “leading modernization of” or “shaping.”
- Add one concrete proof point from recent experience, e.g., “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “3.5M annual page views,” to increase impact.
- Tighten the second sentence by grouping related capabilities and reducing the long list.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading web modernization, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Built and scaled enterprise digital systems for mission-driven organizations, including a 10,000+ page Drupal migration supporting 3.5M annual page views, with leadership across analytics, editorial workflows, multimedia production, and AI-enabled search experiences.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; consider narrowing to “AI-enabled search experiences.”
- “Analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production” repeats later skills sections almost verbatim.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this section overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize distinctive leadership-level capabilities rather than repeating broad phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, concise noun phrases and sharpen wording: “Enterprise web modernization” instead of “Enterprise website modernization.”
- Prioritize the most marketable, recent strengths: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI-enabled search, automation/integration.
- Consider a tighter version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Workflow automation and platform integration • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Keep style consistent by avoiding mixed constructions like “operations” vs. “experiences” unless each item clearly signals a capability area.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences” repeats the header and recent projects almost verbatim.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” and several other items duplicate Topline Skills; consider using this section for broader themes only.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant examples that reinforce the headline, but the block is too dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. It will land better with tighter phrasing, parallel structure, and clearer project outcomes or scope.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a simple lead-in and use consistent action/result phrasing: “Built…,” “Developed…,” “Launched…”.
- Tighten wording and remove filler like “designed for continued campaign growth”; replace with “scalable modular architecture.”
- Standardize style: use “AI-powered” or “AI-enabled” consistently; spell out “10 x 20-foot” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider this rewrite:  
  Recent Projects: AI Hybrid Search — Built an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat. We Are Counties Microsite — Developed a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources, and scalable modular architecture. Organization Anniversary Campaign — Produced a multi-part digital campaign featuring editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and a 10 x 20-foot interactive conference display. Advocacy Video Series — Launched and produced a recurring advocacy video series across web, email, and social.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI search, microsites, and advocacy video closely overlap with current freelance and NACo bullets; keep this section shorter and more portfolio-like.
- “Built/Developed” repeats heavily across the CV; vary verbs where possible.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Website

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear relevance, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the project footer and prior NACo entries. Tighten around scope, seniority, and 2–3 concrete outcomes or flagship initiatives.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact + client scope: “Advise a U.S. national membership organization on digital strategy, enterprise web improvement, and cross-channel content operations.”
- Consolidate execution bullets: combine “digital systems, workflows and analytics” with governance/operating-model language to avoid sounding repetitive.
- Make the Drupal/campaign bullet outcome-led: mention launched microsites, reusable content modules, or member resource hubs if you can quantify usage, speed, or efficiency.
- Recast the AI work as a signature initiative: “Lead AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user-facing discovery experience.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item repeats details already covered in Recent Projects (AI search, microsite, anniversary campaign); keep this entry higher-level and let the project section hold specifics.
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” also echoes the 2022–2024 NACo role; emphasize consulting/advisory scope and current technical delivery.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the strongest achievements into 4–5 bullets, led by the Drupal migration: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-based: add audience growth, engagement, open/click rates, production volume, or cost savings if available; otherwise trim “tens of thousands/thousands” language.
- Strengthen impact verbs and results: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing internal production capacity for advocacy programming, events, and recurring video content”; “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to improve executive decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version strategic, not operational.
- Video/programming language also appears in older NACo entries; emphasize studio build-out and organizational capacity here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Tighten it to emphasize scope, channel ownership, and operational improvements that set up the promotion.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to focus on ownership and progression: “Directed day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy messaging.”
- Combine related bullets and sharpen verbs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing with clearer impact: “Built stronger cross-team editorial planning and standardized digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Improved digital publishing workflows” overlaps with the Director role’s governance/publishing standards; keep this version tactical, not strategic.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; frame this here as scaling/formalizing the program, not originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it largely repeats the header, core competencies, and recent roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level leadership themes and sharper differentiation from the technical and analytics skills sections.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with more distinctive, outcome-oriented phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms
- Editorial governance and cross-team content operations
- Multi-channel communications leadership across web, email, social and video
- Advocacy and member-focused messaging strategy
- Audience-centered content planning and campaign storytelling
- Use “member-focused” instead of “public-sector” if targeting association/nonprofit roles; it aligns better with recent NACo and consulting work.
- Keep wording parallel: noun phrase + scope/outcome, avoiding generic labels like “leadership” alone.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” overlap heavily with Core Competencies and the header.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is broad; if kept, pair it with “campaign storytelling” to make it more specific.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill mix, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and execution themes, not repeat a software inventory.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization,” “Front-end implementation,” “Platform integrations and workflow automation,” “AI-enabled search and structured content experiences.”
- Cut lower-priority or older-signal items here, especially “jQuery,” and move niche tools like Airtable, SharePoint, and Power Pages to Technical + IT only.
- Tighten phrasing for seniority: “HTML/CSS/JavaScript implementation” reads stronger than listing languages individually.
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end web implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Structured content systems and AI-enabled search experiences”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already covered in Core Competencies.
- Most platform names duplicate the Technical + IT section; keep this section more strategic and selective.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for a senior digital leader, but it currently reads as a tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, emphasize strategic application and decision-making rather than repeating platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as outcome-oriented capabilities, e.g.: “Analytics strategy • KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding and leadership reporting • Web behavior and journey analysis • SEO and performance optimization”
- Keep only 2–3 flagship tools here, e.g.: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI/Looker Studio,” and move/remove the rest to avoid list fatigue.
- Replace “Microsoft Clarity” with a broader phrase like “behavior analytics” unless it is especially important for target roles.
- Consider adding a stronger senior-level phrase such as “measurement architecture” or “decision-support reporting.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates both “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization.”
- “Leadership reporting” may overlap with executive-facing strategy already implied elsewhere; “executive dashboarding” is sharper.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and older NACo bullets. Make it more senior, tighter, and aligned to recent leadership-level multimedia work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Operations**
- Replace with tighter, higher-level bullets:
- Broadcast-quality video production and editing
- Livestream and hybrid event production
- Studio buildout and operations
- PTZ camera and multi-camera workflow management
- If you want a more leadership-oriented version, use:
- Multimedia strategy and production leadership
- Broadcast studio and livestream operations
- Hybrid and virtual event delivery
- Video production workflows and post-production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies; vary wording or remove one.
- “Studio operations” and “PTZ camera systems” are useful, but avoid overemphasizing tactical production if targeting senior digital leadership roles.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Use this space to signal depth and recency, especially Drupal, which is central to recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites, governance) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, prioritize by strength/recency: Drupal first, then WordPress/SharePoint, with Power Pages and GitHub Pages last.
- Consider adding version/scope only where meaningful, e.g., “Drupal 10” if that aligns with recent project work.
- Keep this item platform-focused; avoid adding CMS modernization or technical implementation terms already covered elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills: “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Consider trimming one section or making this one more specific to platform proficiency.
- “Power Pages” should be styled consistently as “Microsoft Power Pages” if used elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more current and implementation-focused, emphasizing tools you’ve actively used in recent roles/projects.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End Development & Technical Implementation
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- If accurate, add scope/context instead of only tools: Front-end implementation for Drupal/WordPress, API-based integrations, tag management, edge scripting, and deployment automation
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required; they add little value for a senior candidate

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with Topline Skills: “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery • API integrations.” Keep one version shorter or make this section more tool-specific.
- “Cloudflare Workers” and “GitHub Actions” are useful differentiators; keep them, as they add more uniqueness than the core coding terms.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow automation capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize systems-building, not just PM/chat tools: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira/Asana/Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams”
- Remove weaker or older-feeling tools unless they are current and used recently; Basecamp is the easiest cut.
- If space allows, add a short qualifier for impact: “workflow automation, intake tracking, approvals, and cross-team coordination”
- Consider renaming the heading to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems” to better match the actual mix of tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating them elsewhere without added specificity.
- Jira, Asana, Trello, Slack, and Teams are common tools; keep only those most relevant to recent roles.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses the scale of your email leadership. It should signal enterprise email/engagement capability, not just list platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Enterprise newsletter operations • Audience segmentation • Campaign deployment**
- If accurate, strengthen with scope: **Platforms supporting newsletters and member communications reaching tens of thousands of stakeholders**
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; lead with the most current/enterprise-grade tool.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Engagement” is already implied in Core Competencies and work history; avoid adding generic phrases like “multi-channel communications.”
- Don’t repeat analytics or automation terms here; those are already covered in separate Technical + IT categories.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” and misses a chance to signal level of use or business impact. Tighten it into a cleaner technical stack and avoid generic nouns.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • A/B testing • KPI/dashboard reporting
- Replace “Dashboarding” with “KPI/dashboard reporting” to sound more outcome-oriented and less generic.
- Order by strategic weight/recent usage: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Clarity aligns with the NACo analytics infrastructure work.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this stack to impact in experience bullets instead of adding more tools here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item is nearly duplicated by “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Consider trimming one version or making this one purely tools-based.
- “SEO” and “A/B testing” are broader practices, not tools; keep them only if similar practice-level terms appear consistently across other Technical + IT items.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and reads as setup work rather than concrete contribution. Since this is an older role, keep it concise and emphasize foundational impact without repeating later NACo leadership achievements.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground progression and scope: “Promoted across two digital media roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Tighten the second sentence around 2–3 concrete contributions: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and improved day-to-day publishing workflows.”
- Replace “high-impact” with specifics if available: add volume, audience, cadence, or event scale (e.g., number of livestreams, weekly series length, traffic/email reach).
- Clarify supervision modestly: use “provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” only if people guidance matters for the promotion story.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; differentiate this as launching or early production support.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow/governance language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes/ownership so it adds distinct value without repeating later digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize initiative and scope: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the podcast the lead achievement: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Trim generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a clearer contribution such as “produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes launched, audience growth, internal stakeholders supported, or projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item focused on innovation/research support plus the podcast launch.
- Avoid overstating team leadership here, since stronger leadership evidence appears in later NACo roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a mixed list of software, workflows, and production capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and several work bullets, so it should be tightened to emphasize tools only.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as a cleaner tools list: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator”
